title: Canada Opens Gordie Howe Bridge Without U.S. Officials as Tariff Tensions Escalate
excerpt: The $4.7 billion bridge connecting Detroit and Windsor opens to traffic Monday, but a dispute over toll revenue and new 50% tariffs have turned a milestone into a diplomatic standoff.
body:
• Canada held a ceremony Friday for the Gordie Howe International Bridge without U.S. officials, after cancelling a planned joint ribbon-cutting over President Trump's new 50% tariffs on Canadian goods.
  • The $4.7 billion bridge connecting Detroit and Windsor opens to vehicle traffic on July 27, with a standard toll of $5.75 for passenger vehicles across its 1.5-mile span.
  • A dispute over toll revenue remains unresolved — Trump claims the U.S. will receive 50% of bridge profits, while Canadian PM Carney says no revenue sharing begins until Canada's construction debt is repaid, roughly 50 years from now.

Canada marked the opening of the Gordie Howe International Bridge on Friday in a subdued ceremony without American participation — a stark departure from what was supposed to be a celebratory moment between two of the world's closest allies.

The $4.7 billion bridge, which connects Detroit, Michigan, to Windsor, Ontario, across the Detroit River, will open to vehicle traffic on Monday, July 27. But the milestone has been overshadowed by escalating trade tensions between the two countries after President Donald Trump announced 50% tariffs on a wide range of Canadian imports earlier this week.

"In light of trade action threatened by the United States earlier this week, it would be inappropriate to proceed with a celebratory event between the two countries."

— Jenna Ghassabeh, spokesperson for Canadian Infrastructure Minister Gregor Robertson

A Bridge Mired in Politics

Named after legendary Detroit Red Wings hockey player Gordie Howe, the bridge has been decades in the making. Construction began in 2018, with the project entirely funded by Canada. It was originally scheduled to open in June but was delayed after Trump threatened in February to block the project, citing Canadian provinces' refusal to sell American alcohol, Canadian tariffs on U.S. dairy products, and Canada's ongoing trade talks with China.

https://x.com/globeandmail/status/2080705815523328391

The bridge finally received clearance to open after the U.S. and Canada struck a deal on tolls earlier this month. But Trump's announcement of 50% tariffs on Monday — in response to what his administration called Canada's "discriminatory treatment" of American-made cars, alcohol, and dairy — prompted Canada to cancel the joint celebration.

Windsor Mayor Drew Dilkens and other Canadian officials attended Friday's ceremony, with no U.S. federal or state representatives present.

The Toll Revenue Dispute

The two countries remain at odds over how bridge revenues will be divided. Trump posted on Truth Social that he had renegotiated the deal so that "the United States of America now gets 50% of the Profit." White House spokesman Kush Desai echoed that Trump had secured "an incredible deal for America."

Canadian Prime Minister Mark Carney offered a sharply different interpretation. He said an earlier agreement between Canada and Michigan stipulates that "there's no splitting of tolls under that agreement until all of the debt is repaid" — a timeline he estimated at roughly 50 years.

Nicolas Lamp, an associate professor at Queen's University's Institute on Trade Policy, told Reuters that the draft agreement is deliberately ambiguous: "The U.S. can point to the new agreement that says they will get half of the net revenue, while Canada can say that contradicts the original agreement. It's vague enough that each side can save face and claim they won."

By the Numbers

The bridge spans 1.5 miles across the Detroit River, with towers rising 722 feet. It has six traffic lanes — three in each direction — along with 16 toll lanes and 60 inspection lanes. The standard toll for a passenger vehicle is $5.75. Nearly 15,000 workers were involved in its construction, which used more than 22,000 tons of steel and 500,000 tons of concrete.

The Gordie Howe Bridge is meant to ease congestion at the nearby Ambassador Bridge, which handled $126 billion in trade by commercial truck in 2023 and remains one of the busiest land border crossings in North America.

What It Means for the Indian Community

The Detroit-Windsor corridor is home to significant Indian-origin populations on both sides of the border. Michigan's Indian American community has grown substantially in recent decades, particularly in the Detroit metropolitan area, while Windsor and the broader Ontario region host large South Asian communities. The new bridge offers a faster, more efficient crossing for families, professionals, and businesses that operate across the border.

The broader trade dispute carries implications beyond the bridge itself. Trump's 50% tariffs on Canadian goods could disrupt supply chains that Indian-owned businesses in both countries depend on, particularly in the automotive, technology, and agricultural sectors that are deeply integrated across the border.

What's Next

The bridge opens to traffic on Monday — the same day Trump is expected to visit the Detroit metropolitan area. The toll revenue dispute lacks a formal resolution mechanism, which political analysts say leaves Canada vulnerable to further pressure. Don Abelson, a professor of Canada-U.S. relations at McMaster University, suggested that Carney's administration calculated that simply opening the bridge while managing Trump's demands was the best available outcome.
